documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife. Winter has kept him inside more; walks laps at the community center twice a week with a friend from church. No chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations. No falls. Leg still strong. Wife says memory is about where it was in the fall.
Meds: aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, Biktarvy, latanoprost, donepezil 10.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Strength symmetric, gait steady.
A/P: CAD and prior stroke on aspirin and statin; HTN at goal; BMP today. Alzheimer's stable on donepezil. Glaucoma per ophthalmology. Next visit in summer for AWV.

documents.title: Part D formulary change
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Notice from mail order: his Part D plan moved brand latanoprost to a higher tier; generic latanoprost 0.005% remains covered. Ophthalmology prescribes it; called their office, they will send a generic prescription. Wife informed, no gap in drops.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 05/22/2024.

71-year-old man with open-angle glaucoma on latanoprost, right eye pseudophakic, brought by his daughter for abrupt, severe pain in the left eye starting about two hours before arrival, with a frontal headache, vomiting, blurred vision in that eye and rainbow-colored rings around lights. Light makes it worse and he cannot hold the left eye open. No injury, no fever, no discharge. Background: CAD with prior MI and stent, repaired post-MI VSD, prior stroke, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, HIV on ART, Alzheimer's dementia. NKDA.

Exam: left eye red with marked conjunctival injection and tearing; pupil mid-dilated and nonreactive; cornea hazy; anterior chamber shallow. Right eye unremarkable. Tonometry: left IOP 38 mm Hg.

Assessment: acute angle-closure glaucoma, left eye.
Treatment: pressure-lowering eye drops and IV acetazolamide, antiemetic. Ophthalmology on call evaluated in the ED; pressure falling. Laser iridotomy arranged for the morning. Discharged to ophthalmology clinic.

documents.title: Daughter calling about ED visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Daughter called: father went to the ED Wednesday night with sudden left eye pain and was told it was an acute glaucoma attack. Ophthalmology did a laser procedure on the left eye yesterday. Pain gone, vision clearing, eating normally. She wanted us to know and asked if anything in his regular medicines could have caused it. Told her the eye team will review his list and we will look at the records when they arrive; no changes for now. Follow-up visit booked with PCP in June.

documents.title: Ophthalmology letter: acute angle closure
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Dear colleague, your patient presented to the ED on 05/22/2024 with acute angle-closure glaucoma of the left eye, IOP 38 mm Hg. After medical lowering in the ED, I performed a laser peripheral iridotomy of the left eye on 05/23/2024 without complication. The right eye is pseudophakic with a deep chamber and needs no laser.
Follow-up 05/30/2024: no pain, cornea clear, iridotomy patent, angle open on gonioscopy, left IOP 16 mm Hg. Acute attack resolved. Continue latanoprost both eyes at bedtime for his open-angle glaucoma. Post-laser drops completed. Return as previously scheduled, sooner for any recurrence of pain or halos. NKDA.

events.reason: Follow-up after ED visit for eye

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after the May ED visit for acute angle-closure glaucoma of the left eye; ED record and ophthalmology letter reviewed. Laser iridotomy 05/23, pressure 16 at the one-week check. No eye pain now; vision back to his usual.
Reviewed his medicine list against the eye team's question: nothing he takes is a usual trigger. Daughter reassured.
Exam: vitals as charted. Left eye white, small iridotomy visible superiorly.
A/P: acute angle closure, left eye, resolved after iridotomy. POAG continues on latanoprost. Other problems stable. AWV in August.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Annual visit 07/23/2024. Two years after inferior STEMI with mid-RCA DES and surgical repair of a post-infarction VSD; stroke 05/2023 with full recovery. No angina, no dyspnea walking at his usual pace, no palpitations, no syncope. Brief ED visit in May for an eye problem.
Exam: BP and pulse controlled. Regular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
Plan: continue aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5. Return in one year. Our research group may contact him about a secondary-prevention study.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV with wife. Cardiology in July: stable. Eye pressure good since the laser. No falls this year.
Function: independent walking and dressing, cues for bathing and meals; family handles medicines, money, transport. PHQ-9 2. Sleeping well.
Health care proxy (daughter) reconfirmed; no change in his stated wishes.
Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, pleasant, oriented to person. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Gait steady.
A/P
- CAD, old MI, VSD repaired, prior stroke: aspirin, metoprolol, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril, amlodipine. Lipids today.
- HTN: at goal.
- Alzheimer's: donepezil, neurology early next year.
- POAG: stable. HIV: ID in November.
- Prevention: lung CT September; flu and COVID in October.
RTC 5 months.

reports.text: Annual low-dose screening CT, comparison 09/2023. No pulmonary nodules. Lungs clear. Postoperative sternotomy changes stable. No effusion or adenopathy.

documents.title: Ophthalmology follow-up
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Seen 11/19/2024. Left iridotomy patent. IOP 16 right, 16 left on latanoprost. Fields stable. No further angle-closure symptoms. Continue latanoprost. Return one year.

documents.title: Infectious disease annual note
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body: HIV visit 11/12/2024. Continues bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF with family-supervised dosing. Acetazolamide given once in the ED in May; no ongoing interacting drugs. CD4 570 cells/mm3, viral load not detected. Continue. One year.

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With daughter. Cardiology research coordinator called them about a study for people after a heart attack; they have a screening visit in February and wanted my view. Explained that a trial may give either the study drug or placebo, that he stays on all his usual heart medicines, and that his daughter, as his health care agent, can help him decide and withdraw at any time. They will go to the screening visit.
No chest pain, no breathlessness, no falls.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: CAD and prior stroke stable; HTN at goal; BMP today. Alzheimer's, neurology visit in two weeks. RTC summer for AWV.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Follow-up 02/11/2025 with daughter. Gradual progression per family: more help with daily planning, occasional repeated stories, sleeping through the night. MMSE 17/30 (18/30 in 08/2023). Neuro exam nonfocal; gait normal. Continue donepezil 10 mg. Reviewed the cardiology study with the daughter; no neurological objection. Return in 12 months.

documents.title: Clinical trial enrollment notice
documents.author: cardiology research
documents.body: Notice to primary care physician. Your patient enrolled on 03/06/2025 in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled secondary-prevention trial for adults after myocardial infarction, with consent from the patient and his health care agent. He began the blinded study drug, one dose daily, on 03/06/2025. Please continue all usual medications and do not start new lipid-lowering therapy without contacting the study team. Study visits are scheduled at our cardiology office; the study team is reachable at the number on the patient's wallet card for any adverse event or hospitalization.

documents.title: Study medicine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, this is his daughter. Dad started the study pill two weeks ago. Do you need anything from us? Should mom keep it in the pill box with his other medicines?

documents.title: RE: Study medicine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know; we received the enrollment notice and noted the study drug in his chart. Keeping it in the weekly box is fine unless the study team said otherwise. Bring the study card to his visits so any doctor can reach them.

documents.title: Cardiology research visit
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Study follow-up visit 05/22/2025. 72-year-old man with coronary disease after an inferior MI in 2022 complicated by a ventricular septal defect (surgically repaired), enrolled in March in a blinded secondary-prevention trial. He reports taking the study drug and all his usual medicines every day, and he and his wife are following a heart-healthy diet. No chest pain, no breathlessness, nothing new. He asked how well the study drug works; I explained that the trial is designed to answer that question, that neither he nor we know whether he is receiving active drug or placebo, and that results are shared once the study ends.
Vitals: BP 132/84, HR 78. Exam unremarkable.
Lipids: total cholesterol 190, LDL 110, HDL 45, triglycerides 150 mg/dL.
Plan: continue study drug and usual regimen (aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5). Next study visit in six months.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV with daughter. In the cardiology study since March, study visit in May went fine; their lipid panel then was LDL 110, so not repeating lipids today. Neurology in February: slow progression, donepezil continues. No falls, no ED visits this year.
Function: walks independently; needs help with bathing setup, meals, medicines, money. PHQ-9 3.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, no murmur, lungs clear, no edema. Gait steady.
Colorectal screening: colonoscopy from 2016 would make the next one due in 2026. Given his heart history and dementia, he and his daughter prefer a stool test; FIT kit given.
A/P: chronic conditions stable on current regimen. CMP, CBC today. Lung CT September; fall vaccines October. RTC 4-5 months.

documents.body: FIT negative. Letter sent to patient and daughter. Repeat yearly if continuing screening.

documents.body: HIV visit 11/11/2025. In a blinded cardiology trial since March; study team confirmed no expected interaction with his ART. CD4 650 cells/mm3, viral load not detected. Continue bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF. One year.

events.reason: Head injury after fall on ice

conditions.label: Concussion with loss of consciousness of 30 minutes or less, initial encounter

reports.text: Noncontrast head CT, comparison 05/2023. No acute intracranial hemorrhage. No skull fracture. Chronic encephalomalacia in the right anterior cerebral artery territory, consistent with the known prior infarct. No mass effect. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age.
reports.conclusion: No acute intracranial abnormality. Chronic right ACA territory infarct.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 02/12/2026.

73-year-old man with Alzheimer's dementia and a prior stroke who fell backward on an icy front step this morning and struck the back of his head. He was out for a short time and was alert and answering within minutes. EMS reports he vomited twice on the way in. Here he is a little confused but oriented, with a dull headache that has eased over the past hour. Denies change in vision, seizure or weakness. On aspirin; no anticoagulant. Background also includes CAD with prior MI and stent, repaired VSD, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, HIV on ART, glaucoma. NKDA.

Exam: no focal neurological deficit; speech clear and coherent. Scalp without laceration. Neck nontender.
CT head without contrast: no hemorrhage or fracture; old right ACA infarct.

Observed for four hours: awake, cooperative and walking steadily at discharge, still somewhat tired.
Diagnosis: concussion with brief loss of consciousness.
Discharge: home with wife; head injury precautions; acetaminophen for headache; follow up with PCP within the week; return for worsening headache, repeated vomiting, new confusion or weakness.

documents.title: Wife calling after ED visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called: he slipped on the ice yesterday, hit his head and was seen in the ED, CT okay, told it was a concussion. Slept well with her checking on him overnight. Headache mild this morning, no vomiting since the ambulance, talking and walking as usual. Reviewed warning signs. Visit booked Tuesday with PCP.

events.reason: Follow-up after ED visit for concussion

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife and daughter, five days after a fall on ice with brief loss of consciousness; ED diagnosed concussion, head CT without bleeding or fracture. ED record reviewed.
Since: headache faded to almost nothing, used acetaminophen twice. No vomiting. Family says he is back to his usual self cognitively, maybe a bit more tired the first few days. No new weakness or vision change.
Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, conversant, at baseline per family. Cranial nerves intact, strength 5/5 all limbs, gait steady.
A/P
1. Concussion, improving. Rest and gradual return to usual walks. Return precautions reviewed. RN will call in a few weeks.
2. Fall prevention: the fall was a slip on ice rather than a balance problem; daughter arranging ice melt and a railing check on the front steps.
3. Other problems unchanged.
RTC June.

documents.title: Concussion check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called wife for planned check-in. No headache for over two weeks, no acetaminophen needed. Back to walking at the community center. Sleep and appetite normal. No further falls. Will see PCP in June.

Meds: aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, Biktarvy, latanoprost OU nightly, donepezil 10, study drug (blinded).
Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, pleasant, at baseline. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Gait steady.
A/P
1. Concussion, resolved.
2. CAD with old inferior MI, VSD repaired; history of stroke without residual deficits: aspirin, metoprolol, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril, amlodipine. Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids.
3. HTN: at goal.
4. Alzheimer's disease: donepezil; family support in place.
5. POAG: ophthalmology yearly. HIV: ID yearly.
RTC September for follow-up; AWV after that.
